sentences.text:
Bhuneshwar Sahu @ Feku Sahu vs The State Of Jharkhand
Through Its Chief ... on 11 April, 2023

Author: Rajesh Shankar
Bench: Rajesh Shankar
 1
 In The High Court Of Jharkhand At Ranchi
 W.P.(C) No. 2213 of 2021
 ---
1. Bhuneshwar Sahu @ Feku Sahu
2. Ramdhan Sahu
3. Narayan Prasad Keshri ... ... Petitioners Versus
1. The State of Jharkhand through its Chief Secretary, Government of Jharkhand, Ranchi
2. The Deputy Commissioner, Gumla
3. The Additional Collector, Gumla
4. The District Land Acquisition Officer, Gumla
5. The Project Director, National Highway Authority of India Project, Ashok Nagar, Ranchi .... ...
Respondents Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Rajesh Shankar For the Petitioners : Mr. A.K.
Sahani, Advocate For the Resp. Nos. 1 to 4 : Mr. Sandeep Verma, A.C. to Sr.S.C.-III For the Resp.
No. 5 : Mr. Allen Anton Andrew, A.C. to Ms. Khushboo Kataruka, Advocate Order No. 05 Dated:
11.04.2023

entities.text: High Court Of Jharkhand At Ranchi
entities.label: COURT

entities.text: Project Director, National Highway Authority of India Project, Ashok Nagar, Ranchi
entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text: The present writ petition has been filed for issuance of direction upon the District Land Acquisition Officer, Gumla (the respondent no. 4) to re- determine and pay proper and appropriate compensation to the petitioners in terms with various clauses of sub-section (7) of Section 3-G of the National Highways Act, 1956 (in short, "the Act, 1956") or alternatively to refer the matter to the arbitrator i.e., the Additional Collector, Gumla (the respondent no. 3) to re-determine fair and proper compensation in connection with L.A. Case No. 06 of 2018-19 concerning acquisition of land of village Kumharo within a specified period in exercise of power conferred under Section 3-G(5) of the Act, 1956.

2. A counter affidavit has been filed on behalf of the respondent nos. 2 to 4 stating inter alia that as per the villagers of the concerned mouza including the petitioners, the compensation for acquisition of their respective properties was assessed on lesser valuation and accordingly they raised joint objection before the respondent nos. 4 and 5.

sentences.text:
It has further been stated that the respondent no. 3 has been notified as an Arbitrator by the Department of Revenue, Registration and Land Reforms, Government of Jharkhand vide letter no.
1046 dated 30.12.2015 to determine the quantum of proper compensation for acquisition of the lands and structures under Section 3-G(5) of the Act, 1956.

entities.text: Department of Revenue, Registration and Land Reforms, Government of Jharkhand
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Accordingly, after receipt of the objection, Misc Case No. 06/2021-22 and Misc. Case No. 07/2021-22 concerning the acquisition of land of village Kumharo and Kusumbaha respectively were instituted in which notices were issued by the respondent no. 3 to both the parties i.e. the concerned raiyats and National Highway Authority of India directing them to remain present on 13.09.2021 for deciding the issue of determination of proper compensation.
In pursuance of the said letter, the concerned raiyats and the Project Director, National Highway Authority of India were present.

The respondent no. 3 also called for the copies of sale deeds executed in last four years from the District Sub-Registrar, Gumla vide letter as contained in memo no. 377 dated 04.09.2021 and the valuation chart of village Kumharo and Kusumbaha related to the year 2018.

4. It has also been stated in the said counter affidavit that after hearing both the parties and keeping in view the relevant requirements of law, the respondent no. 3 enhanced the valuation from Rs.2,376/- and Rs.2,057/- per decimal (as determined in the year 2018) to Rs.10,030/- per decimal with respect to the land of village Kumharo and Kusumbaha respectively which is appropriate in the interest of the concerned raiyats including the petitioners.

A copy of order/award as contained in memo no. 1594 dated 14.09.2021 issued by the respondent no. 3 in Misc. Case No. 06/2021-22 and Misc. Case No. 07/2021-22 has been annexed as Annexure-C to the said counter affidavit.

5. At this juncture, Mr. A.K. Sahani, learned counsel for the petitioners, submits that the petitioners are not satisfied with the valuation of land arrived at by the respondent no. 3 for making payment of compensation to the petitioners for acquisition of their respective lands as the respondent no. 3 while passing the said order/award has not duly followed the provisions of Section 3-G(7) of the Act,
1956.

Since the respondent no. 3 functioning as an Arbitrator exercising jurisdiction under Section 3-G(5) of the Act, 1956, has already passed order/award as contained in memo no. 1594 dated 14.09.2021 enhancing the valuation of the land of village Kumharo and Kusumbaha to Rs.10,030/-
per decimal, this Court is not inclined to issue any writ of mandamus to the concerned authorities.

8. It is however observed that if the petitioners are still aggrieved with the valuation of the land arrived at by the respondent no. 3 in the aforesaid award as well as quantum of compensation which would be fixed in terms with the award, they may take appropriate recourse against the same as provided under law.
9.
The writ petition is accordingly disposed of.

(Rajesh Shankar, J.) Ritesh/
